claims.head: The Blue Jackets will send their checkers at Tkachuk
claims.call: The Blue Jackets’ L3 (Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier) spends at least 45% of its 5-on-5 time against the Panthers’ first line.
claims.body: At home, the Blue Jackets keep sending Coyle’s line (Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rick Bowness has been using this group as a checking line on the other team’s top line. Tonight the Panthers’ first line is M. Tkachuk, Bennett and B. Tkachuk.
claims.nums: At home: 45% of this group’s 5-on-5 time against first lines, about 33% with no line matching
claims.gist: At home, Rick Bowness likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Panthers’ first line.
claims.cite: Matchups · Columbus home games this season · 3 games, 35 minutes for this group at 5-on-5

chips.tip: Columbus’s L3 (Sillinger, Coyle and Olivier) at home: 45% of its 5-on-5 time against opponents’ first lines. Matchups, Columbus home games this season, 3 games, 35 minutes for this group at 5-on-5.
With no line matching, this group would face first lines about 33% of the time, about as often as those lines are on the ice.

check.measure: share of Columbus L3's 5-on-5 time against Florida L1
check.rule: held if the share is at or above the home habit; partly if above the no-matching level; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: Fresh legs vs. Tired ones
claims.body: The Panthers played last night and get no rest before this one. Teams in that spot usually get the worse of the chances, so we expect the Blue Jackets to control more of the play than they usually do.
claims.call: The Blue Jackets get a bigger share of the 5-on-5 chances than they usually do.
claims.nums: Florida played yesterday · Columbus had 2 days off · Columbus’s usual share of 5-on-5 expected goals: 52.1%
claims.gist: The Panthers played last night; the Blue Jackets are rested.

claims.head: Talbot’s hold on the Panthers won’t last
claims.body: Since 2023-24, Talbot has been a wall against the Panthers, well above his usual. Fans love a pattern like this, but we checked three seasons of them and they predicted nothing. Don’t be surprised if the Panthers finally get to him.
claims.nums: 6 starts against Florida: .940 save percentage · .900 against everyone else
claims.gist: Don’t read much into Talbot’s record against the Panthers.
claims.call: If Talbot starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .900 than to his .940 against the Panthers.

claims.head: Special teams lean toward the Panthers
claims.call: The Panthers’ power play creates at least their usual 8.4 expected goals per 60.
claims.body: The Blue Jackets’ penalty kill is one of the league’s worst, and the Panthers’ power play is near the top. Discipline matters more than usual for the Blue Jackets tonight.

CBJ.head: The Blue Jackets have a lot going for them
CBJ.body: The two have been about even at out-chancing opponents lately. Florida is on the second night of a back-to-back, while Columbus has home-ice advantage. The Panthers can make it interesting if their power play gets going.

items.text: The Panthers are newly without Jacob Markström and Brad Marchand, and have been without Aleksander Barkov since Oct 1. Akira Schmid is expected to start.
Sam Reinhart has a point in nine straight games against Columbus, and 18 points in his last nine against them.
The Blue Jackets are newly without Emil Andrae, and have had to make do without Ivan Provorov all season.
Matthew Tkachuk has a point in five straight games.
